1 Hermippus “ viciens centum milia versuum a Zoroastre condita indicibus
quoque voluminum eius positis explanavisse „ traditur (Plin, H. N., XXX, 2, § 4).
Ex hac immensa mole paucula fragmenta supersunt (de quibus Mystères de Mithra,
I. p. 33 egi), quorum nonnulla ad astrologiam pertinent. Praeter excerpta in Geopo-
nicis servata, vide Pitra, Anal. sacra, V (1888), p. 163, 35 (Πότε ἑπτάμηνον ἔσται),
p. 174, 35. Cod. Paris. 2417, f. 35, habet capitulum inscriptum Ζωροάστρου περὶ
πολέμου προσδοκωμένου. F. C.
sections.en: 1 Hermippus is reported to have “explained two million verses composed by Zoroaster, with indices also of his volumes having been set down” (Plin, H. N., XXX, 2, § 4). From this immense mass a very few fragments survive (concerning which I have discussed in Mystères de Mithra, I. p. 33), of which some pertain to astrology. Besides the excerpts preserved in the Geoponica, see Pitra, Anal. sacra, V (1888), p. 163, 35 (Πότε ἑπτάμηνον ἔσται ('When it will be a seven-month child')), p. 174, 35. Cod. Paris. 2417, f. 35, has a chapter inscribed Ζωροάστρου περὶ πολέμου προσδοκωμένου ('Of Zoroaster concerning an expected war'). F. C.

summary.headline: Spear-Bearing Planets and Letters
summary.text: Astrological doctrine on spear-bearing planets and their effects on character, authority, dignity, marriage, and fortune, with instructions to judge lunar applications in synodic nativities and full moons. The text then begins a chapter on interpreting delivered letters attributed to Zoroaster, distinguishing deceit from truth and good from evil.
